title: Activity telemetry export and data residency check-in with Hydra Consulting
summary: Hydra wants to validate what admin and operational events Redwood captures, how exports work (formats/targets/throughput), custody of encryption keys (CMK vs Redwood-managed), retention policies and ability to meet regional residency and e-discovery requests. AE+SE walked through export options, KMS integration, retention tiers and proposed a pilot to test 30/90/365 day retention buckets with S3 export and a streaming backup to Splunk for nearline analytics.
action_items: Ethan: prepare sample audit export bundle (JSONL + CSV) that includes admin events and SSO assertions, due 2025-05-26
Maya: send SOC 2 Type II summary and Redwood ISO attestation link, due 2025-05-21
Tom: share Hydra's retention policy doc and legal contact for e-discovery rules, due 2025-05-23
next_steps: Schedule 60m pilot kickoff for export throughput test (Hydra infra + Redwood staging)
Provide KMS integration checklist and customer-managed key (CMK) onboarding guide
Share example S3 presigned pipeline and Splunk ingestion mappings
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Alright everyone thanks for carving out time. quick intros—i'm Maya on AE for Redwood. Ethan's our infra se.
[00:00:12] Lena: hi yes lena here, head of security at Hydra. Tom and Aisha with me.
[00:00:18] Tom: Tom, platform, hi.
[00:00:21] Aisha: Aisha, compliance.
[00:00:25] Ethan: Great. want to confirm agenda: audit log coverage, export targets and throughput, KMS/cmk, and residency/retention. any additions?
[00:00:34] Lena: that covers it. the immediate ask from legal is a clear list of admin events and ability to pull them out for e-discovery. and we need to confirm keys and regional custody.
[00:00:45] Maya: perfect. quick opener: Redwood captures admin activities at multiple layers—console UI changes, API key and token lifecycle events, model deployments, routing & policy changes, role and RBAC changes, SSO assertions, and operator-run actions (manual restarts, scaling). we also capture request metadata: requestor id, IP, region, request headers and partial payload hashes. note: sensitive payloads are redacted by default.
[00:01:10] Tom: when you say 'SSO assertions' are you pulling the assertion JWT or just the event that login happened?
[00:01:18] Ethan: good q. we store the event and a compact assertion footprint—timestamp, subject, issuer, assertion id—without full SAML blob unless customer explicitly enables full assertion capture for debugging. we recommend enabling only for short windows because of PII.
[00:01:34] Aisha: ok that helps. on retention, legal is asking for 7 years for some records but security only needs 365 typically. how flexible are retention buckets?
[00:01:45] Maya: we support configurable retention per category. default audit retention is 365 days, but enterprise plans can set per-event retention—30/90/365/1095/2555 (7 years). longer retention is stored in cold tier and is exportable to your S3 archive.
[00:02:02] Lena: cold tier—do we control the key for that storage? we can't have Redwood-managed keys for certain data types.
[00:02:09] Ethan: yes—two modes: Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys (CMK). for CMK we integrate with common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). we never store the CMK material; we store references and use envelope encryption. key rotation is supported; rotating a CMK does not retroactively re-encrypt older archives unless you request a rewrap job.
[00:02:33] Tom: curious about the export mechanisms. we operate a Splunk cluster and S3 lake. can we stream in near-real-time to Splunk and also have periodic S3 snapshots?
[00:02:44] Ethan: yes. two parallel pipelines: streaming (kafka/pubsub/webhook/Splunk HEC) for near-real-time ingestion and batch export to S3/GS/Blob for long-term archive. streaming throughput is quota-limited per account; if you have bursty admin activity we can autoscale or buffer to an export backlog with guaranteed-at-least-once delivery semantics.
[00:03:06] Lena: about delivery guarantees—if there's a network outage, are exports held locally and retried?
[00:03:11] Ethan: correct. we maintain a bounded local buffer and retry with exponential backoff. we also support resumable S3 multipart uploads for big snapshots. retention of buffered copies is limited and encrypted.
[00:03:22] Aisha: what's the export format? legal wants something easily parsable.
[00:03:28] Maya: exports are available as newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with a schema doc, or as CSV for summaries. JSONL preserves nested fields—SSO assertion footprint, role changes, request metadata. we include a schema version and checksum (SHA256) for each export object.
[00:03:44] Tom: do logs include user email and IP? PII concerns here.
[00:03:48] Ethan: email and IP are captured by default for admin actions, but you can enable pseudonymization—hashing or tokenization—before export. that can be done at export time or as a pre-export pipeline step in your account config.
[00:03:59] Lena: and audit immutability—can entries be altered server-side? we need immutable trails for audit.
[00:04:05] Ethan: audit logs are append-only in our storage tier. modifications create a new metadata record with the operation and the actor who made the change. we support WORM-like export snapshots for legal holds; snapshots are signed and include a manifest, checksums, and a tamper-evident chain.
[00:04:22] Aisha: tamper-evident chain—does that use something like hash chaining?
[00:04:26] Ethan: yes simple hash chaining per-day bucket plus manifest signing using the archive key. for the highest assurance we can provide notarization options—periodic notarized digests to an external ledger (add-on).
[00:04:40] Maya: pricing note—longer retention and high streaming throughput can increase costs. we'll surface estimated unit cost per 10k events per day in the pilot sheet.
[00:04:51] Tom: regarding residency, where are archives stored? we need EU-only for certain clients.
[00:04:56] Ethan: Redwood supports region pinning. for hosted we have region-specific storage (US, EU, APAC). for strict residency we recommend private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where data never leaves your VPC; we can also do EU-only S3 endpoints so exports land in eu-west-1, for example.
[00:05:14] Lena: if we go with CMK in EU, how is key management handled cross-region?
[00:05:19] Ethan: CMKs are region-bound with cloud KMS. cross-region replication requires rewrapping keys or customer-managed replication. we document the steps. for strict residency, avoid cross-region replication.
[00:05:30] Aisha: we sometimes need partial redaction for PHI. is there a redaction pipeline?
[00:05:35] Ethan: yes, we have export transforms—regex-based redaction, tokenization, and a pseudonymization module. advanced PII detection (NLP-based) is an add-on and should be used carefully because of false positives.
[00:05:47] Tom: legal also asked about retention deletion workflows and proof of deletion. can you prove a record was purged?
[00:05:54] Maya: deletion is a two-step process: logical tombstone plus eventual physical purge in cold tier according to retention. we produce deletion manifests with hashes and timestamps; for legal holds you can freeze retention and create a preservation snapshot.
[00:06:06] Lena: on evidence packs—what do you include in an evidence pack for SOC2?
[00:06:11] Ethan: standard evidence pack includes export of admin events for a timeframe, SSO access logs, RBAC change history, config snapshots, and KMS access logs (depending on CMK consent). we also include platform metrics and operator runbooks. pack generation is automated and can be restricted to specific accounts or org units.
[00:06:26] Aisha: about RBAC—are role changes auditable at the granularity we need (who approved, request ticket id)?
[00:06:33] Ethan: yes we tie RBAC mutations to the request context—actor, approver field (if your workflow provides it), and we can ingest an external ticket id field via API. many customers push ticket references in metadata.
[00:06:46] Tom: how do you handle service accounts and machine-to-machine tokens?
[00:06:50] Ethan: service account events are logged similarly—token issuances, rotations, revocations. we emit telemetry that flags long-lived tokens and can recommend rotation windows.
[00:06:59] Lena: curious about on-prem snapshot support—if we deploy Redwood private, can we configure local archival to our object store?
[00:07:06] Ethan: yes private deployments can write directly to your object store (S3-compatible) or on-prem NFS. export controllers run inside your VPC and never pass the archive over public internet.
[00:07:16] Maya: i'll note that for private there's some extra ops for key sync and for the rewrap flow.
[00:07:21] Aisha: ok, one more—metadata search. can we query events quickly across 3 years?
[00:07:27] Ethan: metadata indexing is configurable. hot tier search supports low-latency queries; cold tier requires indexing or restores for full-text. for long windows we recommend shipping a copy to your analytics system (Splunk/Elastic) for fast queries.
[00:07:40] Tom: can you demonstrate a run of export? maybe a small sample so we can validate schemas.
[00:07:45] Maya: yes that's an action item—Ethan will hand a sample JSONL.
[00:07:49] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[00:07:52] Lena: also timeline—legal wants to greenlight pilot within two weeks, is that realistic?
[00:07:58] Maya: yes if we get legal's retention doc and your infra contacts we can kick off in 7–10 business days.
[00:08:06] Tom: what about access controls for exported archives—who inside Redwood can see export contents?
[00:08:12] Ethan: access is restricted with RBAC; exports are only accessible to platform ops and the customer unless a support escalation is opened. all access is logged and included in the audit trail. we also support a read-only evidence access role for auditors.
[00:08:25] Aisha: support escalations—are they recorded and signed off?
[00:08:29] Ethan: yes support-access sessions are recorded and stored in a separate access-audit log with justification and TTL.
[00:08:36] Lena: any gotchas with GDPR data subject requests?
[00:08:40] Maya: we provide tooling for DSAR—mapping events to user identifiers and a purge pipeline that can redact or permanently delete user-attributable entries when legally required, with deletion manifests for proof. note: if records are part of a legal hold we can't purge until hold released.
[00:08:58] Tom: ok that covers most. how do we validate integrity of long-term archives regularly?
[00:09:04] Ethan: we support scheduled integrity checks—checksum validation and rehydration tests. we can publish the schedule and results to your monitoring.
[00:09:13] Aisha: what's the SLA on export availability for the streaming pipeline?
[00:09:18] Ethan: streaming SLA depends on plan; enterprise includes 99.9% delivery success within a 24h window, with retries and backlog durability.
[00:09:27] Maya: to recap next steps: we'll send SOC/ISO docs, Ethan will deliver sample JSONL, Tom will share retention and legal contact, and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff.
[00:09:38] Lena: perfect. thanks.
[00:09:41] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite and materials. bye.
end_notes: Call ended with agreement to run a small export pilot. there were clarifications around CMK rotation and residency; SE to deliver sample and ops checklist. some transcription errors present (Speaker 6 in transcript).
file_notes: Recorded via Fireflies. contains security-sensitive discussion; share only with Hydra's legal and security contacts per confidentiality agreement.
